1: His medical history was notable for moderate intellectual disability, transient neutropenia in childhood that resolved spontaneously, microcephaly, truncal obesity, and joint hyperextensibility of the hands, feet, ankles, and knees.
On examination, his facial features included a thick head of hair, bushy eyebrows, a short upturned philtrum, a high nasal bridge with a beak-shaped nose, and an ogival palate.
Fundus examination showed bilateral disc pallor, generalized arteriolar narrowing, mid-peripheral “bone-spicule” pigmentary changes, and retinal pigment epithelium atrophy.

Thus, the patient presented with a syndromic pigmentary retinal dystrophy characterized electrophysiologically as rod–cone dysfunction with macular involvement, in the setting of high bilateral myopia, presenile cataracts, facial dysmorphism, transient childhood neutropenia, intellectual disability, truncal obesity, joint hyperextensibility, and microcephaly.
